Resources

The publications, open datasets, and software behind the Open Performance Data Initiative (OPDI) — together with the open-source ecosystem the initiative is built upon.

References of the algorithms

The published work, standards, software and data that the Algorithms pages name under Based on. Each page says how its method relates to them: taken from a source, derived in part from it, or comparable to it but developed separately.

Standards and EUROCONTROL methods

  • EUROCONTROL (2017). Airport Collaborative Decision-Making (A-CDM) Implementation Manual, version 5.0, 31 March 2017. Publication page. Defines the 16 A-CDM milestones, among them landing (ALDT, milestone 6), in-block (AIBT, 7), off-block (AOBT, 15) and take-off (ATOT, 16), and the taxi-out and taxi-in times.
  • ICAO. GANP Portal: KPI overview (the key performance indicators of the Global Air Navigation Plan). PDF. Among them KPI02 (taxi-out additional time), KPI05 (actual en-route extension), KPI08 (additional time in terminal airspace, with 40 NM and 100 NM cylinders), KPI13 (taxi-in additional time), KPI17 (level-off during climb) and KPI19 (level-off during descent).
  • Peeters, S., and Guastalla, G. (2017). Analysis of vertical flight efficiency during climb and descent. EUROCONTROL Performance Review Unit, edition 00-04, 19 January 2017. PDF.
  • EUROCONTROL. Point Merge (concept page, with the reference documents of the method). Web page.
  • EUROCONTROL (2026). Point Merge catalogue: an inventory of worldwide implementations, July 2026. Publication page.
  • AirNav Ireland. Irish AIP, ENR 1.5 Holding, approach and departure procedures (AIRAC 14 May 2026). States that holding procedures are based on ICAO Doc 8168 (PANS-OPS), Volume II. Web page.

Papers and reports

  • Olive, X. (2019). traffic, a toolbox for processing and analysing air traffic data. Journal of Open Source Software, 4(39),
    1. doi:10.21105/joss.01518. Software: documentation, source code.
  • Olive, X., Basora, L., Sun, J., and Spinielli, E. (2024). Training a machine learning model to detect holding patterns in aircraft trajectories. Journal of Open Aviation Science, 2(2). doi:10.59490/joas.2024.7943.
  • Olive, X., Waltert, M., and Schultz, M. (2025). Assessing airport surface traffic performance from open sources of aviation data. Air Transportation Research and Development Symposium. Publication page.
  • Proud, S. R. (2020). Go-around detection using crowd-sourced ADS-B position data. Aerospace, 7(2), 16. doi:10.3390/aerospace7020016.
  • Team resourceful-quiver, Delft University of Technology (2025). Fuel consumption estimation. Report of the winning solution of the PRC Data Challenge 2025. Repository with the report.
  • Schäfer, M., Strohmeier, M., Lenders, V., Martinovic, I., and Wilhelm, M. (2014). Bringing up OpenSky: a large-scale ADS-B sensor network for research. Proceedings of the 13th International Symposium on Information Processing in Sensor Networks (IPSN), 83–94. doi:10.1109/IPSN.2014.6846743.
  • Schultz, M., Rosenow, J., and Olive, X. (2022). Data-driven airport management enabled by operational milestones derived from ADS-B messages. Journal of Air Transport Management, 99, 102164. doi:10.1016/j.jairtraman.2021.102164.
  • Sun, J., Ellerbroek, J., and Hoekstra, J. (2017). Flight extraction and phase identification for large automatic dependent surveillance–broadcast datasets. Journal of Aerospace Information Systems, 14(10), 566–572. doi:10.2514/1.I010520.
  • Sun, J., Hoekstra, J. M., and Ellerbroek, J. (2020). OpenAP: an open-source aircraft performance model for air transportation studies and simulations. Aerospace, 7(8), 104. doi:10.3390/aerospace7080104. Software: OpenAP.

Software and data

  • Alligier, R., and Gianazza, D. (2024). Team likable_jelly, winning solution of the PRC Data Challenge 2024 (ENAC). Repository.
  • Goens, Q. (2024). HexAeroPy, a EUROCONTROL Python package that finds the airports, runways, taxiways and stands used by a flight from its positions, version 1.0.4. Repository, package, data (doi:10.5281/zenodo.10651018).
  • Uber. H3: a hexagonal hierarchical geospatial indexing system. Documentation.
  • Olive, X., Basora, L., and Sun, J. (2022). Arrival trajectories at five major European airports. 4TU.ResearchData, version 1. doi:10.4121/20411868.v1.
  • The OpenSky Network. OpenSky REST API: the fields and units of a state vector. Documentation.
  • OpenStreetMap Wiki. Key:aeroway: the tags of airport areas such as runways, taxiways, aprons and stands. Wiki page.
  • OurAirports. Open data downloads (airports and runways, public domain, updated daily). Repository.
  • EUROCONTROL Performance Review Unit. pruatlas: maps and boundaries for PRU publications, including the flight information regions of the Network Manager. Repository.

Publications

Peer-reviewed papers and open datasets underpinning the OPDI and the PRC Data Challenges.

JOAS
2026

Paper

Aircraft Fuel Burn Estimation: The EUROCONTROL PRC 2025 Data Challenge

J. Sun, E. Spinielli, M. Strohmeier

Journal of Open Aviation Science, vol. 4, no. 3

Describes the dataset behind the 2025 PRC Data Challenge, merging ACARS fuel telemetry crowd-sourced through airframes.io with Automatic Dependent Surveillance–Broadcast (ADS-B) trajectory data from the OpenSky Network (OSN).

Zenodo
2026

Dataset

Aircraft Fuel Burn Estimation Data Challenge

J. Sun, E. Spinielli, M. Strohmeier

Zenodo

The open dataset used in the 2025 PRC Data Challenge.

JOAS
2025

Paper

Aircraft Takeoff Weight Estimation: The EUROCONTROL PRC 2024 Data Challenge

E. Spinielli, J. Sun, M. Strohmeier, X. Olive, Q. Goens, R. Koelle, A. Tart, J. Fitzgerald

Journal of Open Aviation Science, vol. 3, no. 2

Introduces the 2024 PRC Data Challenge and the open dataset used to develop models estimating an aircraft’s actual takeoff weight.

4TU
2025

Dataset

Dataset for EUROCONTROL PRC 2024 Data Challenge on Aircraft Take-off Weight Estimation

J. Sun, E. Spinielli, X. Olive, M. Strohmeier

4TU.ResearchData, version 2

The open dataset used in the 2024 PRC Data Challenge.

SID
2024

Paper

The Open Performance Data Initiative: A Foundation Supporting the European Open Science Alliance for ATM Research

Q. Goens, R. Koelle, E. Spinielli, T. Bolić, A. Cook, M. Strohmeier

SESAR Innovation Days 2024

The foundational OPDI paper. Applies a conceptual trajectory reduction approach to publicly available crowd-sourced ADS-B data, producing flight events, measurements, and flight lists covering 33.9 million flights from January 2022 to July 2024.

SID
2023

Paper

Roadmap for a European Open Science Alliance for ATM Research

T. Bolić, A. Cook, R. Koelle, E. Spinielli, Q. Goens, M. Strohmeier

SESAR Innovation Days 2023

Identifies open data as a key ingredient for reproducible Air Traffic Management (ATM) research and postulates the roadmap towards an Open Science Alliance that the OPDI builds upon.

OPDI Software

Open-source projects created and maintained by the Performance Review Commission (PRC) as part of the initiative.

Python

OPDI

The software that produces the OPDI data: a Python package that runs the processing steps on Apache Spark, from the OpenSky Network’s position reports to the published daily files. Processing steps describes what it does, and the Algorithms pages describe each algorithm.

Repository · API reference

Python

OPDI reader (opdi.published)

A small part of the OPDI package that reads the published daily files into pandas tables, gives back the table shapes of release v0.0.2, and creates DuckDB views. It needs pandas, pyarrow and DuckDB, not Spark. See Access for examples.

Repository

Airflow

OPDI daily processing (Airflow)

The schedule that produces the data: two Apache Airflow workflows, one that processes each new day and one that processes a chosen range of past days. They are in the airflow/ folder of the OPDI repository, with instructions for running them.

Repository

Python

HexAeroPy

Determines the airports, runways, taxiways, and stands used by a flight from its coordinates alone. Developed for small-scale applications of the OPDI approach to airport layouts.

Repository

Open-Source Foundations

Open-source projects from the wider open aviation software community that OPDI builds on, or that work well with its data.

Python MIT

traffic

A toolbox for processing and analysing air traffic data, for example to plot and analyse the trajectories of OPDI flights.

Repository · Documentation

Python LGPL-3.0

OpenAP

The open model for aircraft performance and emissions, by Dr. Junzi Sun of TU Delft. OPDI uses its rules and values to decide the flight phase of each position report (see Vertical events).

Repository · Documentation

Python LGPL-3.0

pyopensky

The Python interface to the OSN database, providing access to state vectors and historical trajectories via the REST API and Trino.

Repository · Documentation

Python LGPL-3.0

fastmeteo

A fast tool for obtaining meteorological data along flight trajectories, for example to add weather to OPDI flights.

Repository

Contributing

If you maintain an open-source project that builds on OPDI data, or would like to contribute to one of ours, we would like to hear from you. Contact us at pru-support@eurocontrol.int.
